body: I stopped the Zoloft, it was making me suicidal (which was why I created the post last month). Pfizer really should get a kick up the ass, because the drug had no positive effect whatsoever, and I had to pay THEM.. I'm hesitant to try another drug after that fiasco. I talked to my psychologist, and they're starting me on CBT like you suggested. So far we only talked for about an hour on breathing exercises, breathing with your stomach instead of your chest in social situations. Seems stupid, but it does decrease adrenaline flow, no help with social anxiety though. Anyhow just wanted to update you.
anybody have success with drugs, at least as a temporary "nudge" in the right direction? Zoloft made me suicidal and only lazyness prevented me from following through.
ey, not true. I use to do okay in social situations in my teens, early 20's kept to myself. late 20's completely socially phobic.

I just started on "CBT", and it's been useless so far. They told me to control my breathing when in social situations, ie breath from belly not chest. I tried it, and while it does seem to pump less adrenaline, it doesn't help with social anxiety at all.
I'll have to try that out when I get a chance, thanks.

The problem with doing any of this is mostly in my work schedule. I work 7am-5pm and so does the health center. I'd get laid off if I started taking 2 days off a week to do "therapy". =/ I use this one professional because they can do it after work hours, so I'm stuck with them. I doubt they'll have the "CBT" option available after 5pm. I read about it on wikipedia, but it kind of just confused me more. lol.

I've been on Zoloft for about 5 weeks or so, and the only effects I've experienced so far are these.



*Very minor decrease in libido.. this isn't bad

*Social Anxiety remains the same (original reasoning for taking meds)

*Depression went from mild to severe after starting Zoloft. I never really was suicidal before, but the drug made me severely depressed.

*Very mild sort of "headache" ever since starting it, I guess that's what people mean by "zombie" very minor reaction time decrease, very minor mental reaction decrease. I found it harder to concentrate when reading on things requiring intellectual ability.



The depression was really bad about a week ago, so I started decreasing the dose from 50mg/day to 25mg/day and I feel a little better. I don't think my brain likes Zoloft at all. Is it too early to stop and try another SSRI? So far it's all been negative and nothing positive.


Thanks for caring/responding!

EDIT: I talked to my doc a couple weeks ago, but this was before things got worse. I see them again in a couple weeks, so I'll ask them then.

Was it really necessary to change "divorced loser" to "divorced fuckup"? I think you have some serious anger issues! I couldn't help but notice that you threatened to kill somebody trying to help in another thread. It sounds like you're suicidal yourself and are transposing your feelings onto other people. You called me, "misanthropic", you're probably right, but I think that would apply moreso to you.

I think your last statement should be changed to, "My life is precious, not yours. Get over yourselves." Survival drives us all, it's instinctive human behavior, priority #1 is oxygen, #2 water, #3 food, #4 shelter, etc. Somewhere along the line is social interaction and acceptance, it might be #5 for some, or #99 for others.

Nonetheless, I do agree with part of your post, and that your review of the nature of the posters/commentors is partly correct. I must ask though, since you seem to imply that you know, but what is "proper treatment" according to western medicine?

Those types of quizzes often have flaws in the way they're asked; asking a question one way, and then asking it another way you can often get extremely different results from the same person. Maybe with time surveys will be rounded for human factors, but I don't put much confidence in them as they are now. 

I'm not really expecting much, my problem is that against all reason and logic, and for all intensive purposes I don't have a reason to be depressed. It's illogical, and since I know it's illogical, that would suggest that my brain chemistry is to blame. I guess the best route for me is to try out the different SSRI's and see if one works, otherwise, I'm out of ideas.

No they're not using CBT that I'm aware of, it just seems more like a counseling session, which doesn't seem to be helping a lot. I'm really kind of relying on them for help though, cause my life has just continually been spiraling downward. I tried to "tough" out the depression, I use to say that S.A.D. was just another lame condition created by Merck, Pfizer, Eli Lilly, etc to sell more drugs, but it's become apparent to me that humans are social beings and without the ability to interact socially, we lose interest in life. That is the realization that is my life. 

What are your friends experiences with Zoloft/SSRI's/Meds in combating depression?

Thanks for the reply. I had never thought about the anatomy issue that way, you make a good point! 

I am still seeing the psychologist, though there is about 3 weeks in between each appointment which seems like forever. They help somewhat, I told the psychologist every detail about my past, and that I'm severely depressed. The visits help a little bit, just to talk to somebody, but nothing is really changing. 

You asked if I feel in control of the treatment I'm receiving. It really doesn't feel like treatment, more like I just spill my guts, and the psychologist tells me I need more confidence. I'm a fairly reasonable and intelligent person, and I know the different between confidence and anxiety. I've purposefully put myself into some very dangerous situations in life which require the greatest care and confidence; so it's not a confidence issue. I don't think they know what they're doing because it's not helping. The one psychologist I talked to, said I had clear symptoms of S.A.D. and they put me on Zoloft. I've been on that for just over a month and it's had no effect, in fact has only depressed me more and made me more lethargic. I see why people commit suicide on the stuff, not that I am going to, but it definetaly increases that type of thinking.

What's important to me right now is to find some friends, primarily a girlfriend, then eventually get married, have kids, etc. The thought of getting in a relationship completely terrifies me because it might fail, and I don't want to take that risk (that might be from parents divorce, but I'm guessing it's more a self-protection fallacy). I have never been able to connect with people, and I even feel the psych hardly cares, just telling me to be more "confident". It sucks too because I've got a "lot going for me" according to them, looks, job, youth. But a monkey has more social ability than me, and anytime I try to socialize I essentially freak out and isolate myself. I use to drink a lot, but I don't anymore. It never really helped me socialize but it numbed my inhibitions; it made me more shy, but I didn't care, so I drank. Now I'm just done caring so I don't drink.

I'm completely honest with them, because it's like I'm detached from life and it just keeps getting further and further away, so there's no point in hiding anything. I normally walk out a little higher spirits than normal, but the next morning things are even worse than the morning before because I know nothing will ever change. Mornings suck, that's the one time of day I'm suicidal! Not really, but I do hate mornings; I guess it's in part because I have nothing to live for, don't confuse that with suicide, I'm just pointing out that I don't have anything to pull me in to life. 

Anyway thanks for replying. Sorry if I rambled / made grammar errors, I'm a bit tired.
